title: Declared branches: install asks for the development and release branches and sets GitHub's default branch to match
summary: init now asks for the development and release branches (Enter keeps GitHub's current default), a new branches sub-command records them in config.json and, only on github.com and only from the default the remote reports, creates a missing branch and makes the development branch GitHub's default; check, verify, status and /orion-verify report a disagreement, and the suite runs every gh call against a stand-in with a refusing gh first on its path.
friction: The issue was agent-ready yet its acceptance criteria require an edit to this repository's CLAUDE.md, which a person merges, so the unattended run had to ask the person for leave to merge.

The first approval came in round 3, so its Fix now lines needed a fourth, confirming review; SKILL.md's three-round cap counts rounds without approval and does not say whether a confirming review after a round-3 approval is allowed. The run took it, and the user-visible exception then sent two more fixes to dev with no further review.
lessons_learned: Code that changes a remote setting must read the remote's own current state every time (a stale or missing origin/HEAD is common), name the host explicitly on every gh call (GH_HOST can redirect it), and test the host check against mirror and look-alike URLs up front: rounds 1 to 4 each found one more of these.

deferred.what: In a clone with no origin/HEAD (a git init + git push repo before git 2.48), an init that names no branch on a working branch stores that branch as both names and writes it into the starter CLAUDE.md; the next session then flags GitHub's real default as the mismatch and the offered fix would make the working branch GitHub's default.
deferred.why: Whether that path may make a network call or should store nothing is a design decision.
